_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Burundi covering the Kingdom of Burundi, mwami monarchy, German and Belgian colonialism, Hutu-Tutsi dynamics, 1972 genocide, civil war 1993-2005, and Nkurunziza third-term crisis.

ethnic_groups.name: Hutu
ethnic_groups.notes: Majority ethnic group; traditionally agriculturalists; Bantu-speaking

ethnic_groups.name: Tutsi
ethnic_groups.notes: Historically dominant minority; pastoralist origins; same Kirundi language as Hutu

ethnic_groups.name: Twa
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous pygmy people; oldest inhabitants; hunter-gatherers; marginalised; potters and entertainers

natural_resources.notes: Significant rare earth/nickel deposits (Musongati nickel—one of world's largest undeveloped deposits); largely unexploited mineral wealth; subsistence agriculture dominates; 3T minerals (tin, tantalum, tungsten) conflict mineral concerns

military.notes: Rebuilt post-civil war from ethnically-balanced Hutu/Tutsi integration (Arusha Accords 2000); major AU peacekeeping contributor (AMISOM in Somalia, 5,400 troops); Imbonerakure youth militia (ruling party) controversial

debt_aid.notes: World's poorest country by GDP per capita; heavily aid-dependent; sanctions following 2015 political crisis; HIPC debt relief beneficiary; subsistence economy

education.notes: Free primary education since 2005 (dramatically increased enrollment); Kirundi/French bilingual; chronic teacher shortage; ethnic quotas in universities (60/40 Hutu/Tutsi); conflict disrupted education repeatedly

diaspora_migration.notes: 2015 political crisis produced massive refugee outflow to Tanzania/DRC/Rwanda; DRC refugees also hosted; cyclical ethnic violence since 1972 produced waves of displacement

digital_economy.notes: Lowest internet penetration in Africa; mobile money becoming primary financial tool; VTEL Burundi expanding 4G; very limited tech ecosystem; power shortages hamper digital growth

current_leader.name: Évariste Ndayishimiye
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: CNDD-FDD candidate; took office after death of Nkurunziza

former_leaders.name: Mwambutsa IV
former_leaders.notes: Last mwami (king); fled after 1965 coup attempt

former_leaders.name: Ntare V
former_leaders.notes: Last king; deposed by Micombero; killed 1972

former_leaders.name: Michel Micombero
former_leaders.notes: First republic president; 1972 genocide against Hutu

former_leaders.name: Jean-Baptiste Bagaza
former_leaders.notes: Military coup; modernisation attempts; anti-Church policies

former_leaders.name: Pierre Buyoya
former_leaders.notes: Two terms via coup; opened multiparty system; Arusha Accords

former_leaders.name: Melchior Ndadaye
former_leaders.notes: First Hutu and democratically elected president; assassinated; triggered civil war

former_leaders.name: Cyprien Ntaryamira
former_leaders.notes: Killed in same plane crash as Rwandan President Habyarimana

former_leaders.name: Sylvestre Ntibantunganya
former_leaders.notes: Acting president during civil war; ousted by Buyoya

former_leaders.name: Pierre Nkurunziza
former_leaders.notes: Former FDD rebel leader; third-term crisis 2015; died in office June 2020

910.name: Early Settlement and Bantu Migration
910.description: Twa hunter-gatherers as earliest inhabitants; Bantu-speaking Hutu agriculturalists arrive; later Tutsi pastoralists migrate into the region.

sub_clusters.name: Twa Hunter-Gatherer Communities
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous Twa (Pygmy) peoples as the earliest known inhabitants of the Great Lakes highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration into Burundi
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking agriculturalists settle the highlands; iron-working and farming transform the region.

920.name: Kingdom of Burundi
920.description: Emergence of the Kingdom of Burundi under the mwami; Ganwa princely class; complex social stratification between Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa.

sub_clusters.name: Origins of the Mwami Monarchy
sub_clusters.description: Founding myths of the Burundian kingdom; consolidation of royal authority under early mwami.

sub_clusters.name: Ntare Rushatsi and Dynasty Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Ntare Rushatsi traditionally credited as kingdom founder; Ganwa princes and the ubushingantahe council system.

sub_clusters.name: Hutu-Tutsi-Twa Social System
sub_clusters.description: Complex clan-based social structure; patron-client relations (ubugabire); Ganwa ruling class distinct from both Hutu and Tutsi.

930.name: German Colonial Period
930.description: Incorporation into German East Africa; indirect rule through the mwami; limited European penetration.

sub_clusters.name: Berlin Conference and German Claim
sub_clusters.description: Burundi assigned to German sphere of influence; gradual exploration and treaty-making with the mwami.

sub_clusters.name: Indirect Rule under German East Africa
sub_clusters.description: Germans administer Burundi through existing royal structures; minimal infrastructure development; World War I disruption.

940.name: Belgian Mandate and Trusteeship
940.description: Belgian administration under League of Nations mandate and later UN trusteeship; ethnic identity cards; hardening of Hutu-Tutsi divisions.

sub_clusters.name: Belgian Takeover and Mandate Period
sub_clusters.description: Belgium occupies Ruanda-Urundi during WWI; League of Nations mandate; consolidation of Tutsi chiefly authority.

sub_clusters.name: Ethnic Identity Cards and Hardened Divisions
sub_clusters.description: Belgian introduction of ethnic identity cards rigidifies previously fluid Hutu-Tutsi categories; favouring Tutsi elite in administration.

sub_clusters.name: Road to Independence
sub_clusters.description: Prince Louis Rwagasore's UPRONA party; Rwagasore assassination 1961; independence 1 July 1962 under Mwami Mwambutsa IV.

950.name: Post-Independence Turmoil and Genocide
950.description: Coups, ethnic massacres, the 1972 genocide against Hutu intellectuals, and Tutsi military dominance.

sub_clusters.name: Monarchy Overthrown and Republic
sub_clusters.description: Mwami overthrown 1966 by Captain Michel Micombero; Republic proclaimed; escalating ethnic violence.

sub_clusters.name: 1972 Burundi Genocide
sub_clusters.description: Selective genocide against educated Hutu; estimated 100,000-300,000 killed; mass refugee exodus.

sub_clusters.name: Buyoya and Controlled Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Major Pierre Buyoya seizes power 1987; limited liberalisation; first democratic elections 1993 elect Melchior Ndadaye (Hutu).

950.name: Burundi Civil War
950.description: Assassination of President Ndadaye triggers civil war; Arusha Peace Accords; estimated 300,000 dead.

sub_clusters.name: Assassination of Ndadaye and War Onset
sub_clusters.description: First Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye assassinated October 1993 by Tutsi soldiers; civil war erupts.

sub_clusters.name: Arusha Peace and Power-Sharing
sub_clusters.description: Mandela-brokered Arusha Accords 2000; power-sharing government; ceasefire with last rebel group FNL 2006.

960.name: Nkurunziza Era and Third-Term Crisis
960.description: Pierre Nkurunziza's presidency; controversial 2015 third-term bid; failed coup; repression and refugee crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Nkurunziza Consolidation of Power
sub_clusters.description: Former FDD rebel leader becomes president; initial stability; growing authoritarianism.

sub_clusters.name: 2015 Third-Term Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Nkurunziza seeks unconstitutional third term; mass protests; failed coup May 2015; 400,000+ refugees flee.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Nkurunziza Transition
sub_clusters.description: Nkurunziza dies June 2020; Évariste Ndayishimiye succeeds; cautious diplomatic reopening.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
